title: Quality and accuracy of cardiopulmonary resuscitation teaching in short videos: an analysis across three major short video platforms
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 100 CPR instructional short videos retrieved from three Chinese platforms (Douyin/TikTok, Bilibili, REDnote), scored by two AHA BLS instructors against the 2020 AHA CPR/ECC Guidelines. The paper reports item-level shares of videos containing specific guideline-discordant (erroneous) demonstrations, with a stated denominator of 100 videos. Those are shares of items judged inaccurate against an external ground truth (published clinical guideline), so they qualify as CONTENT. The many other percentages the paper reports (video quality bands, presence of subtitles, audio clarity, absence of contraindication statements, video acceleration, lack of step-by-step explanation) are completeness/presentation quality, not veracity, and are not extracted as prevalence.

estimates.measure_type: % of CPR instructional videos demonstrating incorrect hand position during chest compression (guideline-discordant)
estimates.denominator: 100 adult CPR instructional videos retrieved by keyword search on three Chinese short-video platforms
estimates.definition: The video demonstrated hand placement for chest compression that departs from the 2020 AHA Guidelines (compressing at the midpoint between the nipples rather than the lower half of the sternum)
estimates.misinfo_def: "Potentially inaccurate or erroneous information contained therein is highly misleading and could lead to the widespread dissemination of misinformation"
estimates.source_quote: substantial errors were identified in critical areas such as the extra time spent removing foreign body airway obstruction (67%), and incorrect hand position during compression (62%).
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results; Results 'Evaluation of CPR procedures', p. 3; Fig. 2
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two evaluators trained as AHA BLS instructors rated each video independently on a five-point scoring standard built from the 2020 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC; scores were submitted to two BLS instructors for review and consensus. No kappa or other reliability statistic is reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: Two evaluators searched for relevant videos using the keyword “CPR 视频” on three of the most popular short video platforms in China: TikTok (https://www.douyin.com/), Bilibili (https://www.bilibili.com/), and REDnote (https://www.xiaohongshu.com/explore) from 25 to 28 July, 2024.
estimates.notes: Pooled across the three platforms; the paper gives no per-platform breakdown of error rates. Coded CONTENT rather than QUALITY because the label requires a demonstrated departure from an external clinical ground truth, which a wholly correct video could not receive.

estimates.denominator: 100 adult CPR instructional videos retrieved by keyword search on three Chinese short-video platforms
estimates.definition: The video omitted or incorrectly performed the responsiveness check (shouting in both ears instead of calling out loudly while tapping the shoulders and observing the response), contrary to the 2020 AHA Guidelines

estimates.measure_type: % of CPR instructional videos showing extra time spent removing foreign body airway obstruction (guideline-discordant)
estimates.denominator: 100 adult CPR instructional videos retrieved by keyword search on three Chinese short-video platforms
estimates.definition: The video showed the demonstrator clearing oral obstructions during airway opening, a step the 2020 AHA Guidelines reserve for patients with a clear history of foreign body airway obstruction or repeated ventilation failure

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two AHA-BLS-trained evaluators scored each video independently against a five-point standard derived from the 2020 AHA Guidelines; two further BLS instructors reviewed and a consensus score was reached. No reliability statistic reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: According to the results, 67% of the videos cleared oral obstructions during airway opening, which may not only fail to reduce coughing during ventilation but could also unnecessarily cost valuable time during the CPR process, as evidenced by real-life experience.
estimates.notes: Marked borderline: the label here penalises an inefficient but not factually false step, so it sits close to the QUALITY boundary. Kept because the paper classifies it as an irregular/erroneous practice (Fig. 2) judged against the AHA guideline.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, and why: (a) the smaller procedural-error incidences reported in the same sentence block - incorrect compression rate 15%, incorrect compression depth 6%, failure to observe chest rise and fall 10%, failure to release the nose after ventilation 8% - are additional definition variants on the same 100-video denominator; omitted per R4 (quality over quantity) since three rows already represent this cell, but they are verbatim and extractable if wanted. (b) All non-procedural-content percentages are QUALITY, not veracity: 86% provided subtitles, 4% had spelling errors in text, 9% had deficient audio clarity, 61% demonstrated the full procedure without step-by-step explanation, 92% did not mention contraindications/indications/complications or that CPR success is not 100%, 83% failed to stress the importance of CPR, 13% accelerated repetitive actions, 78% used complete demonstrations or step-by-step explanations. A wholly accurate video can carry every one of these labels, so by the instructions' rule they are QUALITY and no prevalence row was made. (c) Sample-description percentages (86% creators were healthcare professionals, 88% simulated inside a hospital, 94% used a manikin, 62% showed successful resuscitation, 20% included AED instructions) describe video characteristics, not misinformation. (d) The excellent/moderate/poor quality banding is reported only in figures/tables that did not survive PDF-to-text conversion, so no banded share is available. (e) Mean section scores (e.g. resuscitation success rate 2.63 +/- 0.95) are scale means, not shares, so no row per the instructions.

rob.design: Observational cross-sectional content analysis. Frame: keyword search 'CPR 视频' on Douyin, Bilibili and REDnote, 25-28 July 2024; 235 videos retrieved, 135 excluded (99 non-instructional, 12 non-Chinese, 1 paediatric, 23 duplicates), 100 analysed. Coding: two AHA-BLS-trained evaluators rated each video independently on a five-point scale built from the 2020 AHA CPR/ECC Guidelines (90 points for CPR procedures, 25 for non-procedural content), then two BLS instructors reviewed and a consensus final score was set. No inter-rater reliability statistic (kappa or ICC) is reported; the authors acknowledge subjectivity as a limitation. No response rate applies. Single-country, three-platform, single keyword.
rob.item6_quote: Two AHA BLS training instructors developed a comprehensive CPR scoring standard based on the CPR content from the 2020 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC [18–20]. Each scoring criterion used a five-point scale to evaluate the videos in two key areas: CPR procedures, and non-procedural content (including media attributes, presentation methods, contraindications and complications, resuscitation success rate, and importance of first aid), while also highlighting potentially misleading behaviors that require attention.
rob.item10_quote: Ultimately, 100 videos were selected for evaluation and analysis (Fig. S1). ... In details, 67% of the videos showed extra time spent removing foreign body airway obstruction, 66% showed failure to check for responsiveness, and the incidence of incorrect hand position during compression was as high as 62%
